requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: The claim uses signed comparisons and returns `lo` when `x < lo`, `hi` when `x > hi`, and `x` otherwise, for every 32-bit input triple. This matches the stated behavior, including when the bounds are inverted.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: The claim computes the greatest common divisor of the inputs’ unsigned values. It covers every pair, including `gcd(0, 6) → 6`, as required.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: The claim sums the unsigned values from zero up to, but not including, `n`, then converts the result to 32 bits. This matches the specified sum and 32-bit wrapping.

claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, the exported function returns the sum of all nonnegative integers smaller than the input, reduced to 32 bits.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input, interpreted as an unsigned integer from zero through the maximum 32-bit value.
The sum is computed over integers from zero up to, but not including, that value, then reduced modulo 2³² for the returned 32-bit result.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call execution under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The guarantee is exactly the mathematical sum of all integers below the unsigned input, reduced to 32 bits; it does not describe a signed-input interpretation.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the exported function returns the value constrained by the supplied bounds using signed comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit inputs: the value, lower bound, and upper bound.
Comparisons interpret each bit pattern as a signed 32-bit integer. The selected result is one of the original inputs, so no arithmetic wraparound occurs.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call execution under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: This is a signed comparison clamp, but the claim does not require the lower bound to be no greater than the upper bound; for reversed bounds, its nested comparisons define the result.
All 32-bit bit patterns are covered; there are no excluded or invalid integer inputs.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the exported function returns their unsigned greatest common divisor.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as an unsigned integer from zero through the maximum 32-bit value.
Returns their natural-number greatest common divisor as a 32-bit value; conversion to 32 bits wraps modulo 2³², though the divisor is within the 32-bit range.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call execution under every host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The inputs are treated as unsigned magnitudes, even when their high bit is set; this is not a signed greatest-common-divisor guarantee.
